body:
#2030 IS REBASED AND PUSHED — 293da2d0cc, 5199 passed / 0 failed, 0 behind. F3
only; F1 and F2 untouched and still codex's. Stopping there as instructed.

Both conflicts were import-list unions. My first union was too generous — it
carried OrchestratedLeaseReceipt, which nothing uses; the compiler caught it and
it is dropped. I used `aida pr rebase --check` for the prediction and resolved by
hand only after it recommended manual, which is TASK-1416 applied rather than
agreed to.

NOW YOUR F1 FORK. I MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING, and the measurement rules out A.

    update_requirement call sites in aida-cli-lib (non-test)   73
    emit_spec_completed call sites                              8
    distinct provenance strings   auto-bump, reconcile-status, done, queue-done, edit

OPTION A IS THE WRONG SEAM, and not for the layering reason you gave — for a
simpler one. A seam at `update_requirement` sits on 73 call sites of which a
handful are completions. That boundary is "a requirement was written", and the
event means "a spec reached Completed". Wrapping 73 writes to catch 5 transitions
puts the guard on the wrong noun, and every future non-status write inherits a
completion check it can never trigger.

The seam that WOULD be right is a status-transition helper, not a write helper —
something like set_status(backend, req, new, provenance) — because the thing with
one true home is the TRANSITION, not the persistence. That is a real refactor
with a real blast radius and it is not a rework round on a held PR.

SO: B, WITH ONE CHANGE, AND I WANT TO BE HONEST THAT B IS PARTLY SCOPE DISCIPLINE.
An enumeration test does not prevent a fourth path; it makes one visible the
moment it appears. That is most of the value at a fraction of the cost, and it is
the same trick as BUG-1543's complement criterion.

The change: enumerate on the TRANSITION, not on update_requirement. A test that
walks the 73 write sites would be noise. A test that asserts the set of
`is_into_completed_transition` callers equals the set of `emit_spec_completed`
callers is exact — every place that decides "this is a completion" must also
record it. That set is 3 today and the test fails the moment it is 4 without a
matching emission.

WHERE C HAS TEETH AND I AM NOT USING IT AS A DODGE: the five provenance strings
are genuinely caller-knowledge. A seam cannot infer "queue-done" from a write. But
that argues for the seam TAKING provenance, not against a seam existing — so C is
a real constraint on A's shape rather than a defence of the status quo. I am not
claiming C defeats the seam.

I can do the B test now if you want it on this PR, or file the transition-seam as
a follow-up with the 73-vs-8 measurement in it. Your call — and codex holds F1, so
if this belongs in their round rather than mine, say so and I will hand over the
measurement instead of the patch.
subject: #2030 pushed (293da2d0cc). F1 fork answered: A is the wrong NOUN (73 writes vs 5 transitions) — choosing B, enumerating on the transition not the write
